historical_record.description: Excelsior Playground, Russia and Madrid Streets, was dedicated, according to the official list of 1947 recreation bond playgrounds the Recreation and Park Commission entered in its minutes.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved a $6,000 agreement with Richard Schadt Associates, landscape architects, to design a play structure and site improvements for Excelsior Playground at Russia Avenue and Madrid Street.

The Communities of the Outer Mission organization and the Excelsior Youth Club were to celebrate the completion of the summer mural project at Excelsior Playground with a dedication on Saturday, October 16, 1982.

At the request of the San Francisco Old Timers Baseball Association, backed by local merchants and neighbors, the Recreation and Park Commission named the baseball diamond at Excelsior Playground in memory of Bud DeMeyer.

Answering petitions from Excelsior Homestead residents, the Board of Supervisors bought the two-acre site bounded by Persia, Russia, Madrid and Edinburgh Streets for the Playground Commission in July for $21,000; building the playground waited for 1912-13 funds.

A one-story building was put up at Excelsior Playground, with a 25 by 50 foot auditorium and stage, directors' offices, a kitchen, a club room and a caretaker's room in the basement, along with asphalt tennis, basketball and volleyball courts.
The Art Commission approved a mural design by Richard Montez and Alivia Bearchild for the playground at Madrid Street and Excelsior Avenue.
The Art Commission approved Kim Hallinan's mural design for the Edinburgh Street retaining wall of Excelsior Playground, at Russia Avenue and Madrid Street.
